newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher on money policy signal.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher on money policy signal.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher, though back from early highs, on Friday after central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong late on Thursday reiterated his longstanding "stable to loose" monetary policy, brokers said.
The index ended up 61.42 points or 0.85 percent at 7,283.40, off a 7,302.98 high. Turnover was a heavy T$83.6 billion.
Brokers said the central bank's signal was a key factor.
"Governor Sheu's remarks eased previous worries over a possible tightening of monetary policy, boosting sentiment," said George Hou, a fund manager at Jardine Fleming Securities.
Investors recently have worried that the cabinet's approval of a relatively low consumer price index growth target of 3.0 percent for 1997 may lead to a tightening monetary policy.
In Friday's trading, plastics rose most, up 2.52 percent, on late buying, with Formosa Plastics up T$3 to T$71 and China Petrochemical up 80 cents to T$42.3.

Electronics were strong on expected price rebounds for 16 megabit dynamic random access memory chips after South Korea's Samsung, the world's top memory-chip maker, said on Thursday it would cut 16MB DRAM production.
United Microelectronics rose T$1.1 to T$39.4.
"Electronics also performed strongly on buying by foreign funds, which see its sound 1997 profit outlook," Hou said.
Image scanner maker Mustek Systems rose the daily seven percent limit to T$99 on its listing debut.
Asset-backed shares also attracted buying, with Sinkong Spinning and Ta Jung Transport both limit up to T$66 and T$60.5, respectively.
Brokers said they expected a firming trend ahead, but noted that six-year resistance at around 7,300 remains formidable.
For Saturday, a 7,220-7,350 trading range was seen.
